bib.title: AudioGPT: Understanding and Generating Speech, Music, Sound, and Talking Head

question: How can an LLM (ChatGPT) be given the ability to understand and generate speech, music, sound and talking heads and to hold spoken dialogue, without training a multimodal LLM from scratch?
hypothesis: Using an LLM as a general-purpose interface that dispatches to existing audio foundation models, plus ASR/TTS for spoken I/O, is cheaper than training a spoken multimodal LLM and handles many audio tasks.
contributions: We propose AudioGPT, which equips ChatGPT with audio foundation models to handle complex audio tasks.
We outline the design principles and process of evaluating multi-modal LLMs, and test AudioGPT in terms of consistency, capability, and robustness.
Demonstrations present the efficiency of AudioGPT in audio understanding and generation with multiple rounds of dialogue.

method.summary: A prompt-based pipeline: modality transformer (ASR/TTS), ChatGPT dialogue engine with a prompt manager and task handler that picks an audio foundation model and its arguments, execution of that model, then ChatGPT composes the response. Nothing is trained; evaluation is a proposed three-axis human-rating protocol, and the reported experiments are qualitative demonstrations.
method.task: LLM-orchestrated audio understanding and generation with spoken dialogue

datasets.name: Per-task datasets listed in Table 3 (LibriTTS, MUSTC, ESD, CHiME4, WSJ0-2mix, BinauralDataset, AudioCaption, AudioSet, URBAN-SED, LRS3-TED, LJSpeech, Clotho-v2, OpenCPOP)
datasets.source: named only; used to describe the metrics each foundation model would be evaluated with, no results reported

models.name: Whisper, MultiDecoder, GenerSpeech, ConvTasNet, TF-GridNet, NeuralWarp, Make-An-Audio, LASSNet, Pyramid Transformer, GeneFace, FastSpeech 2, MAAC, DiffSinger, VISinger, TSDNet
models.architecture: pretrained audio foundation models, used as tools (Table 1, Table 3)

inference.prompting: Zero-shot; ChatGPT guided with LangChain; prompt manager describes foundation models in natural language. Prompt text not given.

parameters.deployment: audio foundation models need only a flexible NVIDIA T4 GPU on hugging face space
parameters.model_initialisation: audio models are initialised at environment setup or server initialisation for efficiency

metrics.name: Consistency
metrics.definition: AMT raters judge whether the response aligns with the user's intention, on a 20-100 Likert scale (20 completely inconsistent ... 100 completely consistent), with 95% CI

metrics.name: Capability
metrics.definition: per-task metrics of the underlying models (WER, CER, BLEU, MCD, FFE, MOS, SNR, PESQ, STOI, mAP, F-score, FID, LMD, KL, CLAP, CIDEr-D); listed only

metrics.name: Robustness
metrics.definition: subjective user rating on the same 20-100 scale of sessions covering long chains, unsupported tasks, error handling, breaks in context

eval.protocol: Protocol is described, not run: annotators write prompts per task, an LLM paraphrases them, and Mechanical Turk raters score responses. No scores, rater counts or prompt counts are reported.

results.claim: The experiments are qualitative demonstrations rather than measured benchmarks; no consistency, capability or robustness scores are reported.
results.quote: The current manuscript mainly covers the system description, where the experiments are designed more for demonstration.

results.claim: Qualitative multi-turn case: AudioGPT keeps context across a 12-round dialogue covering several audio tasks.
results.setup: single case study, Figure 3, no quantitative score
results.quote: Figure 3 shows a 12-rounds dialogue case of AudioGPT

results.claim: Inference setup: greedy decoding with temperature zero and 2048 max tokens.
results.quote: We use a temperature of zero to generate output using greedy search and set the maximum number of tokens for generation to 2048.

results.claim: Audio foundation models are deployed on a single NVIDIA T4 GPU.
results.quote: The deployment of the audio foundation models requires only a ﬂexible NVIDIA T4 GPU on hugging face space.
results.note: No latency or memory figures given.

limits: Prompt engineering to describe each foundation model in natural language is time-consuming and expertise-required (authors).
ChatGPT's maximum token length limits multi-turn dialogue and user context (authors).
Output quality is bounded by the accuracy of the underlying audio foundation models (authors).
No quantitative results, no baselines, no rater counts; the evaluation protocol is proposed but not run.
Spoken I/O is cascaded ASR/TTS around a text LLM, so prosody and paralinguistics in the query are lost (inferred from the modality-transformation design).

terms.definition: measures whether the LLMs properly understand the intention of a user, and assigns the audio foundation models closely aligned with human cognition and problem-solving
measures the performance of audio foundation models in handling complex audio tasks
measures the ability of LLMs deals with special cases
